name: Heal yourself
summary: On a key the unit mends itself without a healer, and pays for it in time, safety or supplies. Common forms are a short shutdown or channel that heals while the unit cannot fire (often cannot move either, and can be broken off), a small stock of kits or stims that supply points or teammates refill, a heal over time that incoming damage can outrun, an emergency button that puts out fires and ends a disabled state, and a repair that works only once out of combat. Steady healing with no key is the self-repair armour model, and healing by dealing damage is the heal-on-hit weapon trait; only the version on a key belongs here. The levers are how much it restores and how fast, what the unit gives up meanwhile, and how many uses it has.
counterplay: Punish the tell: a unit that shuts down or channels to heal is standing still or not shooting (the Stark's shutdown, Roadhog's breather), so burst it or flank it right then.
Break it off: stuns, knockdowns and hacks end a channelled heal at once, as they end Roadhog's Take a Breather.
Out-damage it: a heal over time loses to steady fire, and a Helldivers stim does not save a soldier who takes damage faster than it restores.
Make it spend its kits, then cut off the refills: limited stocks come back only from supply drops, crates, supporters or the base.
Use anti-heal where the game has it: Overwatch's anti-heal effects stop Roadhog's healing, though not his damage reduction.
Follow up after an emergency fix: Battlefield's extinguisher leaves a vehicle on low health, close to being disabled again, so a second volley soon after finishes it.

other_examples.unit: Vehicle Crew Repair Training (Soviet commander Guard Motor Coordination Tactics)
other_examples.note: One ability of this Soviet commander lets vehicle crews fix battle damage on their own vehicle, but only after the vehicle has left combat, so a damaged tank pulls back and patches itself up where it stands.

sources.title: Guards Motor Coordination Tactics, Company of Heroes Wiki
sources.note: The commander's list of abilities; a short entry.

other_examples.note: Most US vehicles can let their crew climb out. The crew then repairs its own vehicle, and any other damaged vehicle nearby, by itself and can be sent back in afterwards. Getting out takes a few seconds, and until it is crewed again the empty vehicle counts as abandoned, so anyone can steal it. The crew also keeps the vehicle's veterancy. A self-repair that goes through the crew, at the risk of losing the vehicle.

sources.title: Vehicle Crew, Company of Heroes Wiki

other_examples.unit: Eat Tree (Night Elf Ancients, such as the Ancient Protector)
other_examples.note: Night Elf Ancients are buildings that can pull up their roots to walk and fight. On a key an Ancient consumes a nearby tree and regains a large amount of health slowly, over about half a minute; a patch made the heal bigger but slower. The trees around it are its limited kit.

sources.title: Template:Eat Tree, Warcraft Wiki
sources.note: The ability box that the Ancients' pages include.

shooter_analogues.note: A self-heal that runs on its own energy meter: while it runs he regains health quickly and takes less damage, but he can't shoot or use his other skills, and a stun, knockdown or hack ends it at once. Anti-heal effects stop the healing but not the damage reduction, and the meter starts refilling only after a short pause.

Eating it takes about four seconds and restores a large share of health in steps, never above his maximum; he munches loudly and the camera pulls out to third person meanwhile. It recharges after a wait, but only if he was hurt, and grabbing any health pickup at full health refills it. The alternate fire throws it down as a health pack that a teammate, or an enemy, can take instead.

A single-use item for the utility slot: pressing fire with it out heals the soldier at once by as much as a standard soldier's whole health pool, though it restores no shields, and the soldier switches back to the main weapon afterwards. Certifications raise how many can be carried, up to four.

sources.title: Medical Kit, PlanetSide 2 Wiki
sources.note: Its Description field copies the in-game text.

shooter_analogues.note: Each soldier carries a few stims, two at the start of a deployment and at most four. One injection gives a few seconds of very fast health and stamina regeneration, clears status effects and mends limb injuries; since it heals over time, a soldier who takes damage faster still dies, and it cannot stop an instant kill. Resupply drops and crates found in the field refill the stock, and a player can also stim a hurt squadmate.

shooter_analogues.unit: Fire Extinguisher (vehicle specialization, Battlefield 3, Battlefield 4 and Hardline)
shooter_analogues.note: A vehicle upgrade that works only once the vehicle is disabled and burning: it puts the fire out, stops the burn damage and lets the vehicle start recovering, and in Battlefield 4 it also gives back full mobility. Battlefield 3 lifts aircraft back to about a third of their health, while Battlefield 4 ground vehicles recover no further than the point where they are disabled. In Battlefield 4 it fills the countermeasure slot, so a vehicle that carries it cannot also break locks or hide, and a late patch cut its recharge to a few seconds.

sources.title: Fire Extinguisher, Battlefield Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the in-game descriptions for Battlefield 4 and Hardline.

shooter_analogues.note: A common quick-use item that takes a moment to apply and then slowly gives back a little health across about ten seconds. Five fit in one slot; raiders scavenge, buy or craft them, and with the right skill they can craft one during a round.

shooter_analogues.unit: Med Kit and the other regen items
shooter_analogues.note: Health and shield items are used from a quick key. While using one the legend moves slowly and cannot sprint, slide or use another item, but can cancel at any moment. The Med Kit restores all health but takes several seconds, while a Syringe is much quicker and heals far less, so players pick by how much time they think they have.

sources.title: Regen items (reached through Med Kit), Apex Legends Wiki

player_translation.summary: One key heals you, and the price is the point: you stop fighting for a moment, stand still and exposed, or spend one of a few kits. It turns a close escape into a choice: heal now behind cover, or keep shooting and risk it.
as_user: You duck behind cover and press the key. Depending on the variant you shut down for a few seconds while the bar refills, hold a channel you can break off, or use up one of a few kits.

The risk is plain to see: while you heal you cannot fire (or move, in a shutdown), so you heal after a fight or behind a wall, which is how the Iron Harvest wiki advises using the Stark's Emergency Shutdown.
Kit versions make you count: two or three charges, refilled at a supply crate, from a resupply drop or by a teammate.
A burning or disabled vehicle can carry an emergency button that puts the fire out and gets it moving again, buying time to limp back.
as_target: A healing enemy shows a green pulse and a filling ring, and a unit in a shutdown slumps and goes dark, so you know it is helpless right now.
That is your moment: burst it, flank it, or stun it to break the channel.
Kit users show small pips under their health bar, so you can see when an enemy has used its last kit and has to fall back.
teammates: A teammate guarding a shut-down ally makes the shutdown safe; the Stark's own page pairs it with the Ward repair exosuit, whose repairs the shutdown speeds up.
Supporters refill kits and can stand between the healer and the enemy.
Some versions can be shared: the Sandvich thrown down as a health pack, a Helldivers stim given to a hurt squadmate.
The enemy team watches for heal tells and pushes as soon as one starts.
controls: E heals, one counted key: press for a timed heal or shutdown, hold for a channel that ends on release, or press to use a kit.
Moving or firing ends a channel; a shutdown locks you in until it finishes (proposal).
The share variant drops the kit for a teammate on a long press of the same key.
feedback: Clear tells from above: a green ring that fills over the unit, a soft hum or a loud munch, and a shut-down machine going grey with its lights off.
The health bar shows the coming heal as a pale segment, so both sides see how much it will restore.
A distinct snap and a broken-ring flash when a heal is interrupted.
Kit pips under the player's own health bar and a small kit icon over enemies that still have one.
changes_from_rts: In Iron Harvest the shutdown restores little and is meant for after a fight; a player version needs a heal that matters, or nobody gives up a few seconds of control for it.
An RTS player can pull one unit back to repair while the rest fight on; a single player has only that unit, so a shutdown must be short, clearly telegraphed and safer behind cover than in the open.
RTS units heal while their owner looks elsewhere; here the heal must be interruptible or costly, so it does not stall every duel.
Kits need a visible refill route (crates, supporters, the base), since no build queue replaces them.
Passive regeneration stays with the self-repair armour model; this pattern spends a key, so it must feel like a decision.

team_play.notes: Mostly a solo tool. Teamwork comes from guards who cover a teammate while it shuts down or channels, from supporters who refill kits, and from share variants that hand the heal to a teammate.

notes: A timed or channelled heal with interrupt rules, or a counted item with a refill hook.
Edge cases: healing past the maximum (the Sandvich never does), healing while burning or disabled (the extinguisher ends that state first), and which actions interrupt a channel.
Readable tells for both teams are most of the work.
Big instant heals reset duels and make a unit hard to kill alone; channels, kit limits or a recharge that runs only after damage taken (the Sandvich) keep it in check.
With damage reduction on top (Roadhog) it can make a tank nearly unbeatable one on one; keep the heal interruptible.
Heals that work only out of combat (the Company of Heroes 2 crew repair) are safe but may feel useless; tune them so the choice is real.
A green ring and a sound read well from above.
Many small heals at once (a whole squad using kits) blur together; one shared heal look per unit keeps it readable.

variants.name: Shut down to repair
variants.summary: The unit switches itself off for a few seconds: it cannot move or fire while it mends, so it is used once a fight is over or with a guard nearby.

adds_weaknesses.why: While it repairs it cannot move or fire for a few seconds, so an enemy who catches it then gets free shots.

variants.name: Channel a heal
variants.summary: Keep the heal running to regain health quickly while taking less damage, unable to fire; a stun, knockdown or hack breaks it off.

variants.name: Carry a few kits
variants.summary: A small stock of single-use kits, each healing at once or over a few seconds; supply drops, crates or teammates refill them.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 Medical Kit, Helldivers 2 stims, Apex Legends regen items, ARC Raiders bandages

variants.name: Repair once out of combat
variants.summary: A crew repair button that works only once the vehicle has stayed clear of combat for some time.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes 2 Soviet commander (Vehicle Crew Repair Training)

variants.name: Share the kit
variants.summary: The same heal can be thrown down as a pickup for a teammate, or given to one directly, instead of being used on yourself; enemies may grab a dropped one.

variants.name: Emergency extinguisher
variants.summary: Usable only while the vehicle is disabled and burning: it puts the fire out, ends the disabled state and starts recovery, but leaves the vehicle on low health and takes the slot of another countermeasure.
variants.seen_in: Battlefield 3, Battlefield 4 and Hardline fire extinguisher

variants.name: Crew climbs out to fix it
variants.summary: The crew gets out and repairs the vehicle by hand, then climbs back in; while they work the vehicle stands empty and an enemy can take it.
variants.seen_in: Company of Heroes 2 US vehicle crews

adds_weaknesses.why: While the crew is outside repairing, the empty vehicle can be stolen or destroyed.

countered_by.why: An enemy who reaches the empty vehicle while its crew works outside can drive it away.

variants.name: Feed on the map
variants.summary: The unit uses up a piece of the map, such as a tree, to regain a lot of health slowly; what stands nearby limits how often it can do so.
variants.seen_in: Warcraft III Night Elf Ancients (Eat Tree)

adds_strengths.why: Can recover health in the field without a healer or a trip back to base.

adds_weaknesses.why: While it heals it is slowed, unable to fire or standing helpless, and kit versions run out.

countered_by.why: A stun or knockdown breaks a channelled heal before it pays off, as with Roadhog's Take a Breather.
A silenced unit cannot press its heal key, so it has to back off or keep fighting hurt.
Fast hit-and-run units catch it alone while it shuts down or channels, then leave before help arrives.

open_questions: Should a self-heal ever be instant? (Recommended: no; a short channel, a shutdown or a heal over time keeps a tell that the enemy can punish.)
Should kits come back only from supply points and supporters, or also refill by themselves after a long wait?
In share variants, may enemies pick up a dropped heal, as they can with Team Fortress 2's Sandvich?
Ending your own burning or disabled state on a key (the Battlefield extinguisher) links this pattern by the field rules. Should it get its own pattern, paired with the critical-burn armour model?

shooter_fit.reason: Cheap to build and familiar from shooters (Roadhog's breather, med kits, stims, the Sandvich), and easy to read as a green ring; as a generic pattern it fills out cards rather than defining them.
